items.title: Albert Morgan Interview, 1958-08-19
items.q: Kelly said, we were always dropping different clubs

ctx.x: Then when did you go to Boston?

Well, then, right, right after I closed at Jimmy Ryan's, and, uh, then it was during the war then. So this fellow, Sabie Lewis, from Boston, had a very fine little eight piece swinging band. They were all fine musicians. They played a lot of modern and good swing music, see. So, I met him, it was my closing week. We was one block apart. He was at Kelly's stable, and, and I was down to Ryan, see. So, I passed by there, I heard a little band swinging, so I walked in. Kelly said, we were always dropping different…

I played the mix of land, I played swing, and here's this modern jazz coming, says everybody's going to study. I says, well, I'm going to join the rest of them. He says, nothing to do. I didn't do anything in the daytime, so I went on studying. I wound up three and a half years in New England Conservatory, see? And that's why I had very good training. So then we played, I played, it was progressive music. As a matter of fact, I like all music, all types of music. It's all good when it's played good. That's right.…
